Daily Brief

France faced its most significant civil unrest in years as protests over rising fuel prices and deteriorating public services drew 550,000 demonstrators nationwide, with rioting and looting causing widespread destruction in Paris, Marseille, Lille, and Limoges, where a historic town hall spire collapsed in flames [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. President Trump's decision to suspend newly enacted Russia sanctions drew sharp criticism from Ukrainian President Zelensky, who said the measures 'could have helped enormously' as Russian attacks continue to intensify [BBC, Globe and Mail, Al Jazeera]. In Canada, a serious incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright caused multiple fatalities and overwhelmed regional hospitals, with one Edmonton physician describing it as a 'one in every 15- to 25-year disaster' [BBC, Financial Times, ABC Australia]. European diplomats including consuls from Belgium, France, and Poland were attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the West Bank, prompting US Secretary of State Rubio to warn of a 'crisis' and Ambassador Huckabee to condemn it as an 'act of terror' [BBC, Le Monde]. Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital just four days after lung cancer surgery, walking unaided and confirming plans to deliver Sunday's Angelus blessing [BBC, Globe and Mail, Le Monde].

Violent Riots and Looting Sweep France as 550,000 Protest Rising Costs

  • Approximately 550,000 people demonstrated across France against rising fuel prices, cost of living, and deteriorating public services including schools
  • About 1,800 people were arrested nationwide as riots broke out in Paris, Marseille, Lille, Limoges, Lyon, Rennes, and Angers
  • Widespread looting occurred; protesters broke into city halls in Marseille and Lille; a historic town hall spire in Limoges collapsed after being deliberately set on fire
  • Police deployed tear gas and water cannon; President Macron condemned the violence and vowed prosecution of those responsible

Trump Suspends Russia Sanctions as Tensions with Ukraine Escalate

  • President Trump signed an executive order Friday night suspending sanctions on Russia that Congress had passed and he had signed into law in September
  • Ukrainian President Zelensky called the decision 'unfortunate' and said the sanctions 'could have helped enormously' to pressure Russia toward ending the war
  • Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called Trump's order 'an important and truly historic moment'
  • The move comes amid deteriorating US-Ukraine relations following a controversial US deal to import Russian diesel and disputes over military support

Pope Leo XIV Discharged Four Days After Lung Cancer Surgery

  • Pope Leo XIV, 71, left Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday, walking unaided after surgery to remove a cancerous growth from his lung
  • The 90-minute operation on Tuesday removed the lower lobe of his right lung; tests confirmed adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer
  • The Pope will deliver the traditional Angelus blessing on Sunday and his surgeon indicated no clinical reasons to cancel his planned Latin America trip
  • Pope Leo spoke with Russian President Putin on Friday, urging 'dialogue and peace' amid Russia's continuing bombardment of Ukraine
